broad_table_watch._note: Watched a broad rodata span [0x7de000,0x7e4800) covering all four EFFECT_DISPATCH candidate tables (0x45a0/0x67b8/0x7e24/0x98ac) during move execution. FINDING: 0x45a0 is the shared MOVE-FLOW sequencer (core [6,11,5,4,62,65,22,23,58,28] runs for every damaging move, minor move-specific variation), NOT indexed by effectId. The larger tables (0x67b8/0x7e24/0x98ac) are touched only SPARSELY (single reads) at inconsistent large indices that differ by move/state (Steam eff4 -> 0x7e24[339]; Hydro eff0 -> 0x67b8[399]) -- NO clean effectId->index mapping. Consistent with the earlier static disproof. Conclusion: the effectId->seqId 'remap' is NOT a clean single-table lookup; the move effect is applied data-driven within the shared move-flow handlers, consuming the already-extracted move-effect DATA (usum_moves.json status/statChanges/flags/effectId).
